summary: Junior Astronaut is a 3D game where kids ages 7–12 run a Moon base for six days. They decide how to use limited power to make air, grow food, and keep the crew safe. When a solar storm arrives, for example, sending the crew to shelter protects them but leaves less power for other jobs.
details: Junior Astronaut is a 3D browser game built by Team SpaceForAll for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. It puts kids ages 7–12 in charge of a Moon base for six days. Their job is to keep two astronauts safe and make sure they have enough air, water, and food. Players start with an illustrated comic, then walk around the base and make decisions. When a solar storm arrives, for example, they can send the crew to shelter. That protects the astronauts and uses power the base also needs for jobs like growing food. The game shows what happens after each choice. At the end, players get a mission recap and a short quiz to help them explain what they learned. We turned real NASA data into parts of the game kids can see and use. NASA’s Moon map shapes the 3D landscape, and an archived solar storm record triggers an alert. Scout, a rover, sends readings back to the base as glowing signals. Players can also ask Comet, our in-game robot, a question and open the NASA source behind its answer. We clearly label the parts we made up for the game, such as how much power the shelter uses. We built the game with React, TypeScript, Three.js, and Vite. It runs in a browser on computers and phones without an account or special equipment. We used short instructions, touch controls, and guided walks so younger players could get started on their own. Our goal is for kids to finish the mission able to explain one choice they made, what it cost, and why it mattered.
